sun.upright:
Of all the signs the Sun could land on, Aries is one of the two it likes best. The Sun is exalted in Aries, which is the old way of saying it's an honoured guest there, treated nearly as well as in Leo, the sign it actually rules. Leo and Aries are both fire and sit four signs apart, a trine, so the card's warmth reaches you with nothing in the way. You already want to be first, and to be known as the one who started it, and the Sun pours straight into that.

From the inside it feels like permission. The small hesitation that usually sits behind a big move goes quiet, and you get a stretch where being loudly yourself just works. The catch with an exalted planet is that it can get a bit pleased with itself. Aries burns fast, and a Sun this happy can talk you into treating the first bright idea as the finished one. The Three of Wands covers the middle ten degrees of your sign, the stretch the Sun rules, and the man in it has already sent his ships out and is standing on the cliff waiting for them. The sending you're good at. In my experience it's the waiting where Aries wanders off.

At work your pitch carries the room because you believe every word of it, and the real test is whether you're still on the project a month later when it's gone ordinary. In the body there's proper energy back, worth putting into something that builds, a training plan, a regular swim. Start the thing you're lit up about, and on the same day write down the dull step that comes straight after the exciting one.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the exalted Sun tends to go to an Aries Sun's head. The warmth is still there, it's just running hot, and the announcement ends up louder than anything that follows it. Aries doesn't really do slow discouragement, so when this card dims for you it looks more like a flare that's gone by lunchtime, a big morning and a flat afternoon, energy spent before there was anything to spend it on.

At work it's the launch everyone got excited about and then heard nothing more of, and the small sting when someone steadier finished a version of your idea. In the body it's pushing through tiredness on adrenaline and good intentions. Mars rules your sign and likes a fresh fight better than an old job. Go back to one thing you started and give it a dull, ordinary hour with nobody watching, and let it get a little further along than it was.

moon.upright:
Feelings in an Aries Moon arrive at full speed and get acted on before they've finished arriving. Anger especially. You know you're cross in half a second, and you've usually said so in the next. The Sun is exalted in Aries, so this card comes to your Moon as a welcome guest, and what it brings is gladness moving at the same speed, joy that turns up fast and shows on your face before you've decided to show it. Leo and Aries are both fire, a trine apart, and the warmth gets in without any fuss.

What the card asks is that the warm feelings get as much room as the sharp ones. You're practised at letting people know you're irritated. Delight, softness, plain fondness for someone, those you tend to rush past on the way to the next thing, as if they weren't quite worth stopping for. With the Sun here you've got more of them than usual. Mars rules your Moon and likes to be doing something, so it helps to treat a good feeling as something to act on, the same way you would a bad one.

With a partner it's letting them see you pleased with them, in words, when you're so much quicker to let them know you're annoyed. Your body has energy that wants somewhere to go, and a hard walk or a swim will steady you better than anything you could think your way into. There's probably an old friend you're fond of and rarely tell. Ring them and say so, before the feeling moves on.
moon.reversed:
Blocked fire doesn't sit quietly. With this card upside down on an Aries Moon, the gladness the Sun should bring turns into heat with nowhere to go, and you're irritable without being able to say at what. Whoever's nearest gets the short answer. Or it flips, and you go loud and busy and cheerful, because slowing down would mean feeling whatever's underneath.

At home it's the sharp reply over nothing and the guilt an hour later. In bed it's lying there too wired to sleep while the day's small grievances replay. For an Aries Moon the way out is nearly always physical. Find a ten-minute job you can finish with your hands, a drawer, a bike tyre, the weeds by the back step, and let your body register that something got done. The heat usually drains off through the effort faster than it would through any amount of thinking.

rising.upright:
Aries rising walks in already moving, direct and quick and a bit impatient with small talk, and strangers usually decide within a minute whether they like the energy or find it a lot. With the Sun exalted in your rising sign, most of them are going to like it. The confidence you lead with has warmth in it as well as edge, and because Leo and Aries are a trine apart, both fire, the two don't fight. People read you as sure of yourself and good company at once, which isn't always how Aries rising comes across.

From where you stand there's no sense of performing. You're turning up at full volume, and that's honestly what you're doing. An exalted Sun stakes a lot on the first ten seconds, though. You lead with certainty, certainty opens doors, and it also sets a bar you then have to keep clearing for the rest of the meeting. Mars rules your chart and would happily keep clearing it all day. That gets tiring, and other people can see when it starts to.

In a job interview you're the candidate the panel warms to inside a minute, and the work is letting the substance catch up with the entrance. On a first date it's an easy, bright hour in which you did most of the talking. Next time you meet someone new, ask one real question and hold still for the whole answer, including the slow part at the end.
rising.reversed:
Flip the card on an Aries rising and the strong opening misfires. The heat that usually welcomes people comes across as pushy, all confidence and no listening, and someone who might have warmed to you decides you're a lot before they've had the chance to find out otherwise. Or you're having a flat day and turn the volume up to hide it, and people can hear the effort.

New colleagues get the big version of you and quietly brace. A first date hears a monologue and goes home knowing your opinions and very little else. Spend the first few minutes of the next meeting smaller than you want to. Ask one thing, wait through the whole answer, and let the other person put something into the conversation before you add to it. It'll feel slow, and it usually goes better.

sun.upright:
The Sun has no special standing in Taurus. It's a visitor there and picks up the manners of Venus, who rules the sign, so on a Taurus Sun this card's brightness comes in warm and unhurried, a good mood you can settle into. You're here to make something solid and enjoy it without being rushed, and the card doesn't argue with that. What it adds is friction. Leo, the Sun's own sign, is square to Taurus, both of them fixed and both stubborn, and a square is the kind of tension that only eases once somebody moves.

The Sun wants you out and visible. Taurus wants to be comfortable, and left alone with the good thing it's already got. You'll probably feel it as a low pull between showing your work and simply keeping it. Fixed earth can sit on real talent for years and call it patience, when it's nearer to not wanting the fuss of being looked at, and you know that about yourself even if you'd prefer not to hear it. The square won't let that stay comfortable. It's doing you a favour, though it won't feel like one.

At work it's the quietly excellent job nobody knows the half of, and the raise going to someone louder while you tell yourself you never wanted it. With money there's a safe pile and one lovely thing you keep almost buying. In the body it's pleasure, food, touch, rest, and a habit of overdoing the comfort until it goes heavy. Put one finished thing where people can see it, with your name on it. You don't have to sell it.
sun.reversed:
Comfort that won't let anything change is the usual shape of this for a Taurus Sun. The warmth is real, it's just gone still, all of it going into keeping things exactly as they are. You know what you could make or start, you can describe it beautifully, and the describing turns into a way of never risking the thing itself. Venus makes the stuck place pleasant, which is why you can stay in it so long. Or your good mood starts leaning on what you own, and you only feel bright when the money's fine and the fridge is full.

At work it's the reliable pair of hands who stopped putting ideas up, comfortable and a bit bored. At home there's a project half-finished in the spare room, and a course paid for and dropped by week three. Choose the one thing you've been circling longest and give it an hour, and don't judge what comes of it until the next morning.

moon.upright:
Comfort for a Taurus Moon happens in the body. The same chair, a full pantry, clean sheets, being fed and left alone. The Sun comes to your Moon as a guest of Venus, and so the gladness it brings arrives in a shape you can actually take in, warmth you can touch, a good mood that comes up through the senses. You'll feel it in your shoulders before your head has a word for it.

The square from Leo is where it gets complicated. The Sun wants the joy on show, and a Taurus Moon would honestly sooner feel it privately and not be asked about it. When someone says how happy you look, you can feel yourself close a little, wanting to keep the warmth somewhere it can't be disturbed. That protects the feeling. It can also wall it off, so that even the people you love get held a step back from your actual happiness. The Hierophant is Taurus's Major, the card of the way things have always been done, and in a lot of Taurus families love got shown by doing things for people, while saying it out loud was a bit much.

With a partner you show pleasure in them by feeding them and warming the house, and forget to say the plain glad thing. Your body has a real appetite for the good stuff and tends to slide into too much of it when you're content. Next time you're happy with someone, tell them so while it's happening, in so many words.
moon.reversed:
When the warmth won't come on its own, a Taurus Moon reaches for the nearest substitute. The snack, the online basket, the same comfortable evening on repeat. With the card reversed that's most of what's going on, and the mood stays low because none of it is the thing that's missing. Venus makes the substitutes lovely, so you can stay with them a good while. Fixed earth holds the feeling in place, unspoken, until it packs down into a heaviness you just call being tired.

The bank statement tends to notice before you do. Sleep gets longer without getting better, and a partner feels you a step away and can't get a straight word out of you about it. Before you reach for anything, put a hand flat on your chest and finish the sentence 'what I actually need is'. The first answer is usually something to eat. Wait for the second one.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising meets people slowly. Strangers read you as steady and hard to rattle, someone whose calm they can borrow for a while, and with Venus ruling your chart you usually look good without seeming to try. The Sun on that doorway has no rank there and works through Venus too, so what it lends you is an easy warmth that makes a room feel safer with you in it. Nobody's dazzled at the door, and most people relax a bit once you're in the room.

Leo squares Taurus, though, and the square shows up in how you start things. The Sun likes to step forward and be seen beginning, and a fixed earth rising would sooner be sure first and only be seen once it's ready. So you can hold your own warmth back at exactly the moment it would land best, waiting to feel certain. People read you as solid and occasionally as a bit shut. The ones who wait usually find a lot of heat under the calm. Plenty of people don't wait, and to be honest that's a loss on both sides.

At a new job you're trusted early with the steady work and passed over for the visible role you'd be good at. Meeting someone you're drawn to, your slow warm-up can read as lukewarm, and it usually isn't. Smile first, once, before you've decided the person's safe.
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Taurus rising's calm starts to read as closed. The easy front goes still, and people can't tell whether you're content or just unreachable, so they fill the silence with their own guesses, which aren't always kind. Overdone, it turns into stubbornness you can see on your face, the set jaw, the pleasant nod that means no. Or you're on the receiving end, won over by a nice manner and good presentation and slow to check what's underneath.

At work there's a colleague sure you agreed to something in a meeting you only sat quietly through. Buying something big, a car or a kitchen, it's the smooth salesperson you liked and the contract you didn't read closely. Before the next polite yes, ask yourself whether you'd put a date on it. If you wouldn't, say you'll come back to them, and then do.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns are built to be interested in everything and quick about all of it. The Sun holds no rank in Gemini. It visits, and takes its tone from Mercury, the sign's ruler, so the vitality this card brings you comes out as talk and ideas, a warmth that shows up mostly in words. Leo and Gemini are a sextile apart, fire feeding air, an easy link of the kind that helps a lot if you use it and does very little if you don't.

The Sun wants one clear thing to shine on, though, and a Gemini Sun would happily keep six going. The sextile hands you the confidence and the audience, and then it's up to you to point them at something you'll still care about next month. The Ten of Swords covers the last ten degrees of Gemini, the part of your sign the Sun rules, and it's the card of something being thoroughly over. Read gently, it's about letting one version of a plan end properly so another can start. Gemini tends to leave old plans half alive in a notes app, and they crowd the new one.

At work you're the one everyone wants in the room for ideas and the one they quietly worry about for delivery, and you know half of that is earned. In love you're wonderful company and hard to plan a year around. Pick the project you'd be proud to have your name on in a year and give it the best hour of your day, before the others get a look in.
sun.reversed:
The brightness scatters. For a Gemini Sun with this card turned over, the talent doesn't go anywhere, it just runs in all directions, so you're lit up about five things and finishing none, and talking about the work starts standing in for doing it. Mercury gives you a quick tongue and the Sun gives it confidence, and between them you can explain very convincingly why the thing isn't done yet. You half believe it too.

At work it's the update that sounds like progress and doesn't contain any. With friends you're the funny one who's somehow never actually free. Catch the moment you hear yourself being persuasive and not quite buying it. Stop there and say the plainer thing, even if it's only that you haven't started, and don't follow it with a joke.

moon.upright:
Talking is how a Gemini Moon finds out what it feels. A feeling isn't quite real to you until it's been said out loud to someone and turned over a few times. With the Sun here taking its colour from Mercury, the gladness comes through chatty and bright, a mood that needs company to come fully on. The sextile from Leo makes it easy between fire and air, so happiness for you is a shared, spoken thing, usually better for having been told.

The catch is speed. Air moves on quickly, and you can talk a good feeling through so thoroughly that you've filed it before you've properly had it. The good day becomes a good story, the story goes down well, and somewhere in the telling the gladness itself got skipped. Then you're oddly restless a day later with everything apparently fine, and that's usually why. The warmth needs a bit of quiet around it as well as all the words.

With friends you're the bright, easy one to talk to and rarely the one who says the unpolished thing. With a partner a joke tends to cover the tender thing you meant. Sleep is where it shows most, the mind still going at midnight, replaying the good bits and the awkward bits alike. After you've talked a good feeling through, stay quiet for a full minute and see what's still there. Say that part too.
moon.reversed:
A Gemini Moon with the Sun reversed can end up with two voices arguing over every mood. Mercury's chatter, lit too brightly, won't get off the feeling and won't sit with it either. You check the phone forty times, read one more thing, push sleep back again. You're not short of insight. There's just so much commentary running that the feeling underneath can't get a word in.

The signs are a scattered day where you touched everything and finished nothing, long voice notes at odd hours, a jaw held tight. Friends get the running update and your body gets the skipped meal. Give the restless part one contained job. Write the whole worry out by hand on a single page, then shut the notebook and leave it shut. If the page fills, fine. Don't start a second one.

rising.upright:
People meeting a Gemini rising usually get three questions before they get a name. You come across as curious and quick, and the Sun on the face you show has no standing in Gemini and wears Mercury's colours, so the brightness people meet is a lively, verbal one, wit and warmth arriving together. Fire and air get on, and with Leo sextile your rising sign, the quickness and the warmth pull the same way and open doors fast.

The strain is that this card wants a direction picked and something begun, and a Gemini doorway would sooner keep every door ajar. You can open ten of them in a week and walk through none, and from your side they all still feel open, because you could always go back, couldn't you. What you tend to miss is how fast other people's interest cools when the follow-up doesn't come. The sextile makes starting easy for you. It doesn't help much with the follow-up, which is the part people judge you on.

At work it's the brilliant contact made at an event and left in a coat pocket. In dating it's a sparkling first evening followed by a fortnight of clever messages, with nobody suggesting a second. In a new group you're liked at once and known slowly. Of all the things you've said you'll do lately, pick one and put a real date on it.
rising.reversed:
Nobody can quite get a fix on a Gemini rising under this card reversed. The quick, bright front turns slippery, and you get read as charming and maybe not someone to count on, fair or not. Mixed signals go out, and some of them are yours, a light yes the other person hears as a promise. There can be nerves in it too, the easy patter deserting you at exactly the moment you want it.

At work it's the manager who's learned to double any estimate you give. In a new friendship it's the plan that was definite and then wasn't, twice. Slow the opening line down. Say one true thing about why you're there and let the quiet after it stand. If you feel a promise forming in the first five minutes of a conversation, hold onto it until the last five.

sun.upright:
A Cancer Sun builds its life around the people it loves and wants, quietly, to be the one who held it all together. The Sun has no dignity in Cancer and takes its warmth from the Moon, the sign's ruler, so this card reaches you as a feeling first, a glow you notice before you could say what it's about. Leo, the Sun's own sign, sits right next door to yours, and neighbouring signs don't have much in common. Leo wants the light on itself. Cancer wants it on the family. The card is asking whether some of it could fall on you.

Your warmth goes out to other people so naturally that you can run the whole supply on them and never notice you're standing in the shade. From the inside it feels like being needed, which is close to the best feeling a Cancer Sun gets. The ache usually comes later, when you look at everything you've helped into being and can't find much with your own name on it. The Chariot is Cancer's Major, a driver going somewhere under his own power, and it's worth asking where you'd drive if nobody else needed a lift.

At work you make the team run and someone else presents it. With a parent it's the old family job, the capable child, still running things at forty. There's usually a plan you've told nobody. Say it out loud to one person you trust before you've had a chance to talk yourself out of it.
sun.reversed:
Overdone, a Cancer Sun's warmth starts to come with a tally. The care keeps flowing out, and underneath it you're keeping count, of what you gave and who noticed. The warmth can go managing, the hint dropped where a request should be, the sigh doing the work of a sentence, help offered with a small hook in it. Usually it comes from an old fear that a plain ask will get a flat no.

With a partner it's the evening you wanted and never named, and the sulk when they didn't guess. At work it's the credit you angle for sideways because claiming it outright feels too exposed. Find one place you've been steering from behind and ask straight out for the thing. You'll probably get a yes. If you get a no, it's over in a minute.

moon.upright:
A Cancer Moon wants to feel held, and to know everyone under the roof is alright. It's the Moon in the sign it rules, so the need runs deep and it runs old. The Sun comes in as a guest of the Moon here, and the gladness it brings comes through memory, warmth you half recognise, a good mood tied to a smell or a kitchen or a person who isn't around any more. With the Sun in this seat, a Cancer Moon can feel safe enough to be happy without checking on everyone first.

Leo and Cancer are neighbours with little in common, and you can feel that. The Sun would have you take the warm feeling out into the open and let it be seen. Your instinct is to keep it in, behind the shell, where nothing can knock it. Each sign has what the other lacks, and the card is lending you a bit of Leo's willingness to be glad in daylight, if you'll take it. Most Cancer Moons are better at being happy for other people than at being happy in front of them.

With a partner it's letting them see you soft and pleased, and not only steady and coping. Your sleep and appetite will show how safe you feel. With family an old warmth may come back, a good memory you share with someone. Ring them, and bring it up.
moon.reversed:
With this card upside down, a Cancer Moon starts keeping a file. Every slight goes in with its date, and a story about what the other person really meant gets gone over until it hardens into fact. Or the words give out completely, and you pull into the shell and wait to be guessed at. Neither gets you the holding you're after, and part of you knows it.

In a friendship it's the three-week quiet over something the other person doesn't know they did. At home it's the meal cooked in pointed silence. The story feels airtight because you've rehearsed it so often, which is a good reason to doubt it. Before you act on it, check one fact with the actual person. Quite often the feeling belongs to someone from years ago, and the person in front of you has walked into it.

rising.upright:
Strangers tend to meet a Cancer rising at an angle. You feel out the mood before committing to it, and people read you as gentle and a little guarded. The Moon rules your chart, and in Cancer the Sun works through the Moon as well, so the brightness people meet is soft and tuned in, warmth that's already noticed how they're doing. It's welcoming in a careful way, and kept close.

The Sun likes to start things in the open where people can watch, and a Cancer doorway finds a public start faintly exposing, like turning up somewhere and realising you're the first one there. Leo, right next door, has exactly the nerve you're short of, and the card is offering you some of it. You're very good once you're in, warmer and funnier than that wary first minute suggested, and people are often surprised by the gap. The trouble is how many chances go by while the first minute gets going.

At work it's the role you'd be excellent in and won't apply for cold. Socially it's the group you've been asked to twice and haven't gone to, because you wouldn't know anyone. In a new romance you wait weeks for them to say the first real thing. Think of one opening that needs you to introduce yourself first, and do it while you've got the nerve. You can retreat afterwards if you want to.
rising.reversed:
Cancer rising with the Sun reversed lets caution take the door. Your front goes changeable, open one day and unreachable the next, and new people can't tell which version they're going to get. You might be testing them before you've shown them anything, or sending signals you're sure are obvious while they pick up nothing at all.

A new colleague takes your quiet for disapproval when it's only shyness. Someone you like reads your retreat after a good evening as lost interest, and drifts off. Chances to start something keep passing while you wait to feel safe enough, and that feeling is slow to arrive by itself. Pick one new person and tell them plainly, in a sentence, what you're hoping for. Send it after one read-through.

sun.upright:
With a Leo Sun this card comes home. The Sun rules Leo, so there's none of the usual translating and no borrowing another planet's manners. The card speaks with the authority of a landlord on his own land. Strength is Leo's Major, the woman with her hands on the lion, and the Sun is the planet behind both cards. For you this reads close to a plain description of what you're like when things are going well.

The trouble with being this at home is that there's nothing to push against, and Leo can coast on warmth. When it works you're generous without trying, people feel brighter for being near you, and the confidence is earned. When it tips, the warmth starts needing an audience, and you can feel the difference from the inside, that small drop when you're pleased about something and nobody's there to see you be pleased. Pride sits right in the middle of it. A Leo Sun would sooner make a large, dignified fuss about the wrong thing than admit a small true thing stung, and I'd guess something's come to mind already.

At work you shine under recognition and go quietly flat when the praise dries up. In love you need to be adored, and there's an odd emptiness when you're merely, steadily loved, which is worth thinking about. With a younger person you mentor or raise, your warmth genuinely lights them up. Do one generous thing nobody will ever know you did, and see whether the good feeling lasts without a witness.
sun.reversed:
Left unchecked in its own sign, the Sun gets loud about itself. For a Leo Sun that means a need to be the brightest thing in the room, and generosity that grows a price tag, given partly to be seen giving. You can tell it's happening by how a day feels when nobody claps, flat and faintly cheated. Or pride shuts it down the other way, and you're bright and busy and fine, and nobody's allowed near the sore spot, including the people who could help.

At work your reputation is running a size larger than your output, and you can feel that gap even if nobody's named it. With friends you take the story over and tell it better than the person it happened to. Carry one piece of work all the way through with nobody watching the process, and don't mention it until someone else notices.

moon.upright:
Warm attention from someone who matters is what feeds a Leo Moon. Being noticed, being chosen. The Sun drawn onto it is in the sign it rules, so it lands at full strength with nothing to dilute it, and your feelings go big and bright and easy to read. When you're happy the whole house hears about it. When you love someone you want them to know it in capital letters.

With the Sun at home there's little to soften it, and fixed fire is slow to let anything go, a warm feeling or a grudge. The tender spot is pride. Admitting that a small thing hurt you, a forgotten message, a party you weren't asked to, feels beneath you, so you make a grander, safer complaint about something else and the real one goes unanswered. What you need is usually smaller and simpler than the version you'll let yourself ask for.

With a partner it's the row about the dishes that's really about not being properly looked at all week. With friends you're the generous host who then lies awake counting who didn't say thank you. After a slight there's a heat in the body that won't settle, and sleep comes late. Say the small version out loud to one person. 'I was hurt you didn't ask me' is plenty, and much easier for them to answer.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, a Leo Moon goes looking for an audience and then resents the one it finds. Every feeling turns into a performance and each hurt into a good story, told well and told often, until the telling quietly replaces what happened. Or pride slams it shut, and you're sunny with everyone except the one person who could reach you.

Friends notice the story's been told three times to three people, and got a little better each time. A partner notices you're warm with the whole world and cool with them. Sleep goes shallow. If one person actually hurt you, tell that person the plain version once, no flourishes. Then stop retelling it to anyone else and see how long the feeling lasts when nobody's feeding it.

rising.upright:
Leo rising arrives as if expected, and usually it was. People meet warmth and a touch of theatre, someone who's going to improve the evening by being there. The Sun rules your rising sign, so the brightness you lead with is your own, with nothing borrowed about it, and you can feel people respond, which is part of why you keep turning up at full strength.

The risk with something this at home is a reliable act. You learn what goes down well with a new crowd and you do it, and it works, and after a while people have seen the act a dozen times and still haven't met you. Being admired and being known are different things, and a Leo Ascendant tends to settle for the first because it arrives so much faster. From the inside the applause feels like connection. It can end up standing in for the slower version, where someone gets to see you when you're not on.

In an interview the charm sails through the first round and meets a harder question in the second that charm can't answer. On a first date it's two lovely hours with neither of you saying anything quite true. In a new team people like you in a day and take a lot longer to rely on you. Next time you meet someone, drop the opening line you know works, ask them something you actually want to know, and let it be a bit awkward.
rising.reversed:
The entrance outruns the person making it. For Leo rising with this card reversed, it's big arrival, big warmth, easy confidence to get you through the door, and then people wait for the follow-through the entrance seemed to promise. Or the confidence deserts you and you run the act on autopilot, saying the lines, hoping nobody spots the gap between the glow and how you actually feel.

At work it's the pitch that won the client and the colleague now stuck delivering it, who's started to mind. Socially you're the life of the room and go home feeling oddly unseen, which is a lonely kind of tired. In the next few first meetings, promise a little less than you know you can do, and let people be pleasantly surprised by the rest.

sun.upright:
Most Virgo Suns I know are prouder of being useful than of anything else, and The Sun is a card about being seen. The Sun has no dignity in Virgo and takes its cue from Mercury, the sign's ruler, so the warmth arrives practical, a brightness that wants a job to do. Leo and Virgo are next-door neighbours with little in common, one wanting to be looked at and the other wanting to be of use, and the card is offering you a bit of Leo's ease with attention, which you're usually short of.

The Sun says be visible and enjoy the credit. A Virgo Sun would honestly prefer the work to speak for itself while you stay usefully out of frame. The Eight of Pentacles covers the first ten degrees of your sign, the Sun's share of Virgo, and it shows someone at a bench getting steadily better at a craft. That's your kind of joy, the improving, getting it right. The Sun only adds one thing, which is that at some point you're meant to look up from the bench and let the work be admired with your name on it.

At work your report is better than anyone's and a week late because it wasn't perfect yet. With money there's a careful budget where the one spend on yourself, a course, a good tool, a proper break, keeps missing the cut. Send one piece of work out at ninety per cent, on purpose, and see whether anyone notices the missing ten.
sun.reversed:
Turned over for a Virgo Sun, this card finds every flaw going, usually your own first. The warmth goes cold and exacting. There's a private tally of mistakes running late into the evening, and a careful edit of someone else's work while yours sits untouched. It can pass for high standards. Mostly it's a way of making sure you're never the one being judged.

At work you're fixing a colleague's email while your own project hasn't moved in a month. At home your partner has stopped asking for help because the help comes back with notes. A good habit tightens into a rule you keep failing. Go one whole day without correcting anybody, yourself included, and put the energy you save into one small thing of your own.

moon.upright:
When the drawer's sorted and the plan's been checked, a Virgo Moon can finally relax. Mercury rules your Moon, and the gladness the Sun brings here is quiet and practical, a mood that steadies while you're being useful. When you're anxious you clean the kitchen, and honestly, it helps.

The snag is that Mercury in Virgo can take a feeling apart down to the last screw. You know exactly why you're upset, you could list the causes in order, and knowing hasn't warmed anything. Leo, next door, has the one thing you're missing here, the willingness to enjoy a good feeling without checking it over first. The card lends you a little of that. It'll probably feel unearned, and you're allowed it anyway. The Hermit is Virgo's Major, and a lot of Virgo Moons do their feeling alone, with the door shut, when a bit of company would help.

Your body often shows it first, a tight stomach, skin that flares, sleep broken at three with a list running. With a partner you show love by sorting their tax, and never quite say you were lonely last week. When you catch yourself tidying for the second time in a day, stop and ask what it's really about. Write the answer in one line and don't edit it.
moon.reversed:
Worry gets a promotion in a Virgo Moon under the reversed Sun. Mercury, turned inward, audits everything you feel. Was the reaction reasonable, is the tiredness something serious, did your friend mean it that way. There's a lot of thinking going on and very little comfort coming out of it, and the routines that usually settle you start to feel like rules you keep breaking.

Sleep shows it first, then digestion, then your patience with the people who love you. A partner might hear the fifth question about the same small thing and not know what to say. Take one routine and do it badly on purpose for a week, the bed unmade, lunch unplanned, and notice what happens, which is usually nothing at all.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising looks composed and a little held back, the person who's already noticed your shoes, the typo on the menu and where the exit is. Mercury rules your chart, and the Sun borrows Mercury's manner here as well, so the impression you make is sharp and credible, and people trust you to be accurate. They'll hand you the detail, the logistics, the contract to read before anyone signs.

It's a real asset, and it can box you in. This card is about beginning and being seen to begin, and a Virgo doorway would sooner be fully ready first. Leo sits one sign over with the nerve you tend to lack, the willingness to be looked at before you're perfect, and the Sun is nudging you to borrow some. What people meet is careful and helpful, and quite often they don't meet your ideas at all, because the idea got edited before it reached your mouth.

At a new job you're handed all the admin in week one and still doing it in year three. In a friendship you're the reliable one and rarely the one people ring for a laugh, though you're genuinely funny. Buying a flat or a car, you spot the clause that saves everyone money and nobody thanks you. In the next meeting, say your idea before you say your correction, and let it be rough.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising can read as cold with this card reversed, because the accuracy is doing all the talking. The effort goes into not making mistakes and none of it into reaching the person in front of you, so you hear yourself correcting someone you've only just met. Or you're so careful you say almost nothing, and they fill the silence with their own guesses about what you think of them.

A new manager might take your questions as doubt. A date might take the precision as judgement. That isn't what you meant, and it's how it's landing. Loosen one thing on purpose. Let a small mistake stand in a message, or tell a story before you've got it straight, and see whether anyone minds.

sun.upright:
The Sun is in fall in Libra, and for a Libra Sun that one fact decides most of this reading. Fall is where a planet is least at ease, and Libra sits opposite Aries, where the Sun is exalted. The Sun's natural way of working is direct, in the open and about you, and it runs against the grain of a sign built to consider everyone else first, so the warmth has to go the long way round. Leo is sextile to Libra, an easy link, which is why charm comes readily. It's plain self-assertion that costs you.

You want things fair and pleasant, and you want to be liked while you make them so, which is harder than it sounds. From the inside there's a real difficulty in shining on your own behalf. You can argue brilliantly for a friend, a cause, a partner, and go strangely quiet the moment the thing on the table is what you want. Libra is a cardinal sign, a starter, and your own Major, Justice, holds a sword as well as the scales. The weighing you're superb at. Bringing the sword down, choosing, saying this one's mine, is where the fall bites.

At work you're the diplomat in every dispute and never quite push your own proposal through. With friends it's the trip you organised for everyone and didn't enjoy, because nobody asked where you wanted to go. Take the decision you've been politely stalling on, set a date for it, and tell the people it affects kindly and without a long apology.
sun.reversed:
For a Libra Sun with the card reversed, charm becomes a way of never being pinned down. You're lovely company and you tell people what they'd like to hear, and the cost comes later, in the agreement you didn't mean, the favour you'll quietly resent, the opinion you swallowed to keep the evening smooth. It stacks up over months, and people end up liking you a lot without being sure what you think about anything.

At work you're agreeable in the meeting and privately annoyed at the outcome. In a relationship there's a resentment that seems to come from nowhere and has been saving itself up for ages. Find one honest thing you've been rounding off to keep the peace and say the whole of it, gently, to the person it's about.

moon.upright:
Discord gets straight into a Libra Moon's body. What you need is peace, and more exactly you need the people you love to be getting on. Libra is where the Sun falls, which matters here, because the Sun's instinct is to put you at the centre and a Libra Moon settles by putting the relationship there. So the gladness this card brings reaches you through other people, a table where everyone's happy, and it's real, and it's also a way of never quite finding your own.

The sextile from Leo is the easy part, warmth going out to others without effort. The harder part is the fall, the Sun struggling to shine on its own account, so you can spend a whole evening making sure everyone's alright and go home unable to say how you are. Venus rules your Moon and wants things harmonious, and a feeling you smoothed over for the sake of the peace doesn't disappear. It goes quiet, and turns up later as a headache or a flat mood you can't trace.

With a partner you're always the first to reach across after a row, and you ask nothing back. With friends you read every message twice for tone and keep the group calm. After even a good social evening there's a heavy tiredness from all that invisible balancing. Next time you're annoyed, let yourself be annoyed for an hour before you start working out why they did it. Their reasons will keep.
moon.reversed:
Feelings turn into negotiations. You keep looking for the fair version, the right tone, the reply that upsets nobody, and a Libra Moon with this card reversed ends up drafting its emotions like an email to a difficult client. The fall makes the Sun wait for permission at the best of times. Or you can't tell what you feel at all, because every feeling seems to need someone else's sign-off first.

With a partner it's asking what they'd like for dinner five times and being secretly cross at the answer. With friends there's a message rewritten so often it no longer says anything, sitting there unsent. Your shoulders hold it after a perfectly nice visit. Next time someone asks how you are, give a short true answer and don't soften it with a joke.

rising.upright:
Libra rising arrives graceful and easy to talk to, the one who does the introductions and remembers everybody's name. With the Sun in fall in your rising sign, this has a particular flavour. The card's usual move is to make the entrance about you, and a Libra doorway makes it about the two of you instead. The sextile from Leo keeps real warmth in it, so first meetings tend to go well. The warmth is aimed outwards, though, and you can disappear inside your own good manners.

Libra is cardinal and the Sun is a card for beginning, yet a Libra Ascendant tends to open by mirroring, matching the other person's tone and pace and sometimes their opinions, so well that you lose track of what you came in to say. The Sun in fall won't push you to the front. You have to do that part on purpose, bringing your own view in early and letting it differ from theirs a bit. Venus rules your chart and she'll make even a disagreement sound pleasant, so you've less to lose than you think.

In a negotiation it's the deal that felt friendly and left you with less than you wanted. On a first date it's being so tuned in to them that they learn almost nothing about you. Before you next meet someone new, decide one thing you want out of it, and say it in the first ten minutes however nicely the rest is going.
rising.reversed:
All surface is the risk for Libra rising with the card upside down. The charm goes up and the substance goes down, and people leave a first meeting having liked you and unsure what you said. You may be handing each person the version of you they'll like best, which is exhausting to keep up and tends to catch you out when two of them compare notes.

At work two colleagues find out you agreed with both of them. Socially there are invitations you accepted to be polite and now can't face, and excuses you're inventing to get out of them. When you're introduced to someone new, say one thing you actually think that they might disagree with, say it calmly, and let them disagree.

sun.upright:
Getting to the bottom of things is what a Scorpio Sun does, and not being fooled on the way. The Sun has no standing of its own in Scorpio and takes its colour from Mars, or Pluto if you use the modern ruler, so on you its brightness comes out sharp and private and a bit relentless. Leo, where the Sun lives, is square to Scorpio. Both are fixed signs and both are slow to bend, and a square is friction that only resolves when somebody acts. It's two strong wills arguing inside one person.

The card wants everything laid out in the open, warmth given freely where people can see it, and a Scorpio Sun would prefer nobody saw the table at all. Showing warmth can feel like handing someone leverage. I've seen a lot of Scorpio Suns who are extraordinarily kind in private and would be mortified to have it known. The Six of Cups covers the middle ten degrees of your sign, the Sun's share of Scorpio, and it's a surprisingly tender card, two children and a cup full of flowers, an old kindness remembered. All that guarding usually started out as looking after someone.

At work you're the one who reads the whole contract, and occasionally the colleague others find slightly unnerving. In love you know your partner's moods better than they do and keep your own sealed. Take one thing you've worked out and give all of it to the person it would help most, with nothing held back for later.
sun.reversed:
What a Scorpio Sun knows becomes leverage when the card turns over. It gets kept for later, the secret held because it might come in useful, the test a friend doesn't know they're sitting, the long silence arranged so someone else says too much. It works, often very well, and it leaves you alone in a way that's hard to admit.

At work it's the information you sat on until it could win you something, and the trust that drained off once people felt it happening. In love there's a memory for every wrong, filed and dated. Ask what you're holding in reserve and what the holding costs. Then hand one piece of it over, plainly, to someone who'd be glad to have it, and don't keep score of what it gets you.

moon.upright:
Loyalty, privacy and the truth, roughly in that order, are what a Scorpio Moon needs, and it feels everything at full depth while trusting very few people with any of it. The Sun visits your Moon's sign with no rank there and takes on Mars's colouring, and what it offers is words for the deep water, a bit of daylight let down into feelings that usually stay under. For a Moon that often runs too big to speak, being able to name a thing is a lot.

The square from Leo is the friction. The Sun wants the feeling brought up where it can be seen, and a Scorpio Moon guards it precisely because it matters. Fixed water holds on, so a hurt goes down and stays down, sometimes for years. The Six of Cups falls in your sign, in the ten degrees the Sun rules, and it's all old memory and tenderness. It points at where this softens, the one or two people you'd actually let close, and the bits of childhood warmth still worth going back for.

With a partner it might be finally saying what one particular silence of theirs does to you. With family there's the old thing nobody names, and the relief when one person does. Your dreams may get unusually vivid for a while. Choose the person you trust most and tell them one true thing you've never said out loud. Keep it short. You can say more another time.
moon.reversed:
The words go underground. With the Sun reversed on a Scorpio Moon, the mind starts interpreting where it would usually speak, reading every message for what's hidden in it, sure it knows what's happening in someone else's head and never checking. Fixed water keeps the suspicion airtight, and that's what makes it hard to shift.

It shows up as a jealousy nobody can argue with, or a silence at home that everyone feels and nobody names. Sleep goes restless and the three in the morning thoughts get very convincing. Someone you love may be walking carefully around you without knowing why. Ask one direct question about the thing you've been interpreting, and take the answer at face value for a week before you decide what it really meant.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising comes across as watchful and hard to read, and people often feel seen by you before they've said much. The Sun on your Ascendant is Mars's guest here, with no title of its own, and what it gives you is a banked warmth, confidence that doesn't announce itself. You say little. What you do say lands, and you've usually read the room before it's read you.

The square from Leo is where it pulls. This card is the open hand, everything on show, and a Scorpio doorway gives nothing away until it's sure. So first meetings go one of two ways. When you decide to let a bit of warmth out, it goes remarkably well, because it's such a contrast with the reserve that people feel it twice over. When you stay behind the glass, people come away wary, and they won't tell you they were. The Six of Cups, the Sun's decan in your sign, suggests the way in, through something warm and ordinary, a bit of your own history.

At an interview your answers are short, exact and faintly unnerving to the panel. In dating you're magnetic in the first hour and hard work by the third date if nothing opens up. In the next conversation with someone new, offer one ordinary personal thing early on, your weekend, a book, the town you grew up in, small and true and given freely.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising, with the Sun reversed, can let reserve harden into suspicion. You read every newcomer for their motive, and people can feel themselves being weighed from the moment they sit down. Or you give off a charge you didn't intend, and your silence gets taken for judgement when it's only caution.

At work new colleagues keep their distance, and you read the distance as proof they're hiding something. In friendship you test people before you'll let them near, and lose the good ones who don't enjoy being tested. With a new neighbour it's the wave you didn't return, and the months of nodding it took to undo. At your next first meeting, say what you honestly think about the conversation you're having, out loud, a bit sooner than feels comfortable.

sun.upright:
The Sun and Sagittarius get on about as well as a planet and a sign can without any formal title between them. Sagittarius gives the Sun no dignity, and it takes its tone from Jupiter, the sign's ruler, so its warmth comes out large and generous. Leo is trine to Sagittarius, fire to fire, four signs of open road, so confidence and optimism run together with almost nothing in the way. A Sagittarius Sun is here to find out what it all means and say so out loud, and the card is all for it.

With so little friction you can shine on the vision and skip the follow-through, believing the idea is as good as done because you can see the whole shape of it. The big picture feels like the achievement. You describe the book, the business, the move overseas, and the telling gives you the same lift the doing would, so the doing gets put off. Jupiter makes everything bigger, including the gap between what you've promised and what you've built. Temperance is Sagittarius's Major, an angel pouring carefully from one cup into another, and careful pouring is what the plan is short of.

At work you've got the best vision in the room and the flimsiest plan, and a real chance of getting the vision taken seriously if the detail gets done. In love you describe a grand future with real feeling and never once cost it. Take the idea you talk about most, write down the next three physical steps, each small enough for an afternoon, and do the first before you mention it to anyone.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, a Sagittarius Sun can oversell. Jupiter swells everything, and reversed that means the sweeping claim with nothing under it, the opinion stated as fact, the plan that's mostly enthusiasm, the story that grows a bit each time you tell it. You believe it while you're saying it, which is why other people believe it too, for a while.

At work your big announcements have started getting a polite nod and no follow-up questions. With friends there's the trip you've all been planning for three years. In love you describe a future beautifully and haven't taken a step towards it. Choose one thing you've said you'll do and either do the first part of it or say out loud that you won't.

moon.upright:
Room to move is what a Sagittarius Moon needs, and something to look forward to, and a sense that life is bigger than the week in front of it. Jupiter rules your Moon and colours the Sun too, so the gladness this card brings is big and warm, the mood that comes with a plan to go somewhere, or the first clear day after a grey stretch. The trine from Leo makes it easy. Joy for you arrives quickly and fills the place.

The easy fit hides a small problem. Your emotional habit is to feel a thing hugely, find the meaning in it and get moving again, and the Sun here happily backs the getting moving. What goes unfelt is anything that asks you to stay still. When something hurts you reach for the philosophy, everything happens for a reason, it'll all work out. The philosophy is often true. It's also a way of not sitting with the ache, and the ache comes back as restlessness, a sudden urge to book a flight or quit something.

With a partner you're cheerful about a problem that's genuinely bothering you, and you want space the moment the conversation gets detailed. With friends you're always up for an adventure and hard to reach when things are dull or sad. Your body wants to move, and walking it off honestly helps. So walk it off, and on the way back name the exact moment that set you off, in as much detail as you can remember.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, a Sagittarius Moon preaches at itself. It takes a feeling and builds a sermon out of it, so you know what you ought to feel and you've got the philosophy ready, while the actual hurt or fear sits unattended under the lecture. Jupiter is generous with meaning, and upside down it hands you more of it than the feeling needs. Or restlessness takes the wheel, and you keep moving so you never have to look at any of it.

At home plans get changed at short notice, and a partner gets tired of never knowing where you'll be. With friends you tell the funny version of a bad week so well that nobody thinks to ask how you are. Before the next big change, sit for ten minutes and say exactly what you're trying to get away from. Say it to someone if you can.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes in open and friendly, a bit loud, up for anything, and people warm to it fast. Jupiter rules your chart and the Sun on your Ascendant wears Jupiter's colours, so the brightness you give off is generous, a sense that something good might happen because you turned up. Leo is trine to your rising sign, fire to fire, so the warmth and the confidence back each other up and doors open easily.

The catch is scale. A Sagittarius doorway goes big by instinct, the bold statement, the funny exaggeration, the broad plan, and the Sun's confidence turns all of it up. You promise the earth at a first meeting because in the moment you mean it, and then you quietly dread the follow-up email. There's often a blunt streak too, the true thing said a beat too plainly for the company. People remember how easily you got something started, and they tend to judge you later on whether it got finished.

At a new job everyone loves your energy in the first week, and by the sixth the emails have gone unanswered. Travelling, it's the booking made in a hurry with a condition you didn't read. In a new friendship you invite someone to something wonderful on impulse, and they wait to see if you meant it. Before you say yes to the next big thing, ask one practical question, even if it takes a bit of the shine off.
rising.reversed:
First impressions go wrong in a particular way for Sagittarius rising with this card reversed. The big easy talk that usually opens doors comes out as bluster, or as the blunt thing said in exactly the wrong company. Or you overpromise so warmly that people feel let down later by the ordinary size of what you can deliver. Jupiter rules your chart, and a reversed Sun gives it too much to work with.

At work it's the client who remembers what you promised better than you do. Socially it's the joke that landed badly with someone you'd only just met, and the apology you never quite made. Slow the first five minutes down. Ask a question, listen to the whole answer, and promise nothing until the second conversation, however much you'd like to.

sun.upright:
Building something that lasts, and being respected for it, is what a Capricorn Sun is here for. Saturn rules Capricorn, and the Sun, with no standing there, takes on Saturn's seriousness, so its warmth comes out practical and strategic, the kind that knows how a system works and where the lever is. Leo is quincunx to Capricorn, five signs apart, and the two have nothing in common, so there's a constant small adjustment going on between the part of the Sun that wants to shine because it's enjoyable and the Capricorn part that wants a reason and a result.

The two sides don't naturally talk to each other, and you end up running a negotiation between them. A Capricorn Sun tends to treat every idea as a commitment, so it doesn't try many, and the ones it does try get done properly and a bit joylessly. The Four of Pentacles covers the Sun's decan of Capricorn, from 20 to 29 degrees, and it's a card about holding tight to what you've got. That's the risk here. You keep your light so carefully banked, saving it for when you've earned it, that you forget what you'd even shine on if nobody was marking you.

At work the plan is working, and there's a side idea you dismissed as not serious enough. With a parent or someone senior there's the old habit of still trying to earn their approval with results. Give yourself one small project with no purpose at all, something you're allowed to be bad at and nobody gets to see, an hour a week.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun with this card reversed can go cold and calculating. People start getting measured for their usefulness, and conversations turn into negotiations to be won. The skill's all still there, it's just gone chilly. Or it works the other way, and the warmth stays locked up because you've decided you're not senior enough or qualified enough yet to let it out.

At work you wait for a permission you don't actually need, or take credit a touch too efficiently. At home the evening goes on work email because that feels safer than talking to anyone. With friends there's a catch-up you keep postponing until things calm down, which they don't. Do one thing you'd do if you already held the title you're working towards.

moon.upright:
Being able to cope is where a Capricorn Moon feels safe. Things under control, handled. The Sun picks up Saturn's colouring on your Moon, so the gladness it brings is quiet and earned, the satisfaction of a hard thing finally managed. You deal with a feeling by working out what to do about it, which is often genuinely wise, and people come to you in a crisis because you'll have a plan before they've stopped crying.

The quincunx from Leo is where the strain is. Leo would have you be openly and warmly glad, and a Capricorn Moon finds unearned joy faintly suspect, so you keep adjusting, letting a bit of warmth out and pulling it back. The Four of Pentacles, the Sun's decan in your sign, shows a man holding a coin tight against his chest, and that's your habit with feelings too, keeping them close in case letting them out costs you something. It rarely costs what you think. A lot of Capricorn Moons learned early that being capable was the safe thing to be.

With a partner you show love by handling things, and you're slow to say you needed holding yourself. With family you're still the responsible one long after anyone asked you to be. The tension sits in your jaw and shoulders. Let one person see you not coping, once, and notice what they actually do.
moon.reversed:
Coping hardens into a wall. With the Sun reversed on a Capricorn Moon the warmth gets rationed so tightly that even you can't get at it, and you carry on being capable while something underneath goes grey. You tell people you're fine in a level, reasonable voice, and the trouble is they believe you, so nobody comes.

At work you stay late because home means feeling things. With a partner you're sure you're showing affection through all the responsible acts, and they just wanted you to sit down with them. Physically it's the tight jaw, the shallow sleep, the sense of running on duty. Tell one person, in plain words, how heavy it's been, and let them help with one small piece of it.

rising.upright:
People tend to assume a Capricorn rising is older or more senior than they are, and they decide you're serious and capable before you've said a word. Saturn rules your chart, and the Sun on your Ascendant works through Saturn too, so the warmth you lead with is understated, competence first and charm some way behind, the kind that gets you trusted with something important in a first meeting. Nervous people calm down around you, and that's worth a lot.

Leo is quincunx to Capricorn, and it's an awkward join. The card asks you to step forward and be seen enjoying yourself, and a Capricorn doorway would sooner earn the right to be looked at first, so you hold the warmth back behind the competence and let it out in careful amounts. The Four of Pentacles, which is the Sun's decan in your sign, shows the habit clearly enough, guarding what you've got so closely that people meet the reserve long before they meet what's under it. Some of them give up waiting.

At a new job you're given responsibility early and thought slightly unapproachable. Socially you're respected quickly and befriended slowly, because you make people work for the warm version. On a first date it's a dry, careful hour that only thaws near the end. Let some warmth show earlier than feels professional, one real laugh, before you've decided the person's earned it.
rising.reversed:
Cold, or a bit superior, is how a Capricorn rising can read with this card upside down. Saturn on the doorway makes you look unimpressed, as if you're judging the room from a height you didn't mean to take, or so buttoned-up that people assume you disapprove of them. Or you armour up entirely, all competence and no give, and warmth can't get in or out.

A new colleague reads the flat expression as dislike. Someone interested in you reads caution as rejection and stops trying. Chances that needed a bit of visible warmth go by while you stay correct and contained. Early in the next first meeting, give one small human thing away, a real reaction or a bit of enthusiasm, before you've worked out whether it's safe.

sun.upright:
Leo and Aquarius sit directly opposite each other, and the Sun is in detriment in your sign, which shapes everything here. An Aquarius Sun wants to be its own person and to make things better for the group, both at once. The most solar things a person can do, shining as an individual, wanting the light on them, being the warm centre, all run against the grain of a sign that puts the group and the principle first. The effort shows. That's how the Sun works in your sign, and there's nothing wrong with you for it.

An opposition is the same axis seen from each end. One end says be gloriously yourself, and the other says it isn't all about you. From the inside it can feel like a low guilt about wanting to be seen, so you route your warmth through causes and groups and other people's needs, and do genuinely good work there, while the plain wish to shine on your own account gets treated as slightly embarrassing. The pull of an opposition is towards balance, so you're allowed both ends. Most Aquarius Suns I've read for find the Leo end the harder one to admit to.

In a job you tend to be the person who can see how it could be fairer or smarter for everyone, and who forgets to make sure your name's on it. In love you're warm about people in general and a bit cool up close. Put your own idea forward as yours, and don't hand the credit round to make it easier.
sun.reversed:
Being different can turn into a position. With this card reversed, an Aquarius Sun's warmth cools into contrariness, holding an opinion partly because the room doesn't, keeping enough distance that nobody can pin you down. The Sun is already working against the grain in your sign, and upside down the effort of warming up stops seeming worth it. It looks like independence, and a fair bit of the time it's also a way of never having to be plainly, awkwardly warm with anyone.

At work a good idea gets framed as a challenge to everyone else's, so people resist the tone and never get to the content. With friends you're in the group and slightly above it, observing. In love, closeness gets kept at arm's length with cleverness. For one conversation drop the position, and just agree with someone warmly and out loud where you actually do agree.

moon.upright:
Nobody gripping too tight, and room to think. That's most of what an Aquarius Moon needs to feel safe. Aquarius is the sign of the Sun's detriment, opposite its home in Leo, so the warm, expressive gladness this card usually brings has to work against your natural setting, which is cooler and more even and most comfortable a step back from the heat. You feel plenty. It just tends to go through your head before it gets anywhere else.

Part of you, the Leo end of the axis, wants to be adored and central and unashamedly warm, and an Aquarius Moon finds that wish slightly alarming. So it gets thought about and kept at a manageable distance, admired in other people and resisted in yourself. You can be marvellous with a whole group and oddly stiff one to one, warmer in theory than in the moment when somebody actually wants to hold you. Saturn is your Moon's traditional ruler, and it likes things kept in their place, feelings included.

You need space at exactly the point your partner wants closeness, and both of you read it wrong. With friends you're loyal and reliable and rarely let anyone see you rattled. Without enough time alone you get a nervy, wired feeling with nowhere to go. Let one person past the distance, tell them a plain feeling with no analysis attached, and stay in the room while they answer.
moon.reversed:
With this card upside down, an Aquarius Moon can decide that feelings are messy and best handled from a distance. The detriment bites harder reversed. You go up into your head and explain your emotions to yourself, and the numbness that follows gets called being fine. The warmth the Sun should bring is still around. You're just standing well back from it, and so is everyone who loves you.

With a partner it's the sudden pull away just as things get close, and them left baffled. With friends you're there for everyone's crisis and share none of your own. The body carries the effort of holding people off, a restlessness that won't say what it's about. Come down out of the analysis for one conversation and say the raw version, I'm hurt, I'm scared, I missed you, and let it be awkward.

rising.upright:
On sight, Aquarius rising reads as a little different, friendly without being exactly warm, interesting, hard to place, quite often the most individual person in the room. Aquarius is where the Sun is in detriment, so the easy warmth it wants to lend you has to push against a doorway that keeps a cool, even distance by instinct. What people meet is bright and slightly impersonal, warmth aimed at everyone and no one in particular.

Leo sits directly opposite, and the pull between the two is right there at your front door. The card wants you to walk in and beam at somebody, and an Aquarius Ascendant would sooner be interesting than adored. So you give people the ideas, the wit, the friendliness, and hold back the bit that would let them feel singled out. From your side it feels like not wanting to make a fuss of yourself. From theirs it can read as cool, and they aren't always sure you liked them.

At a party you're the one everybody found fascinating and nobody felt chosen by. In a new job your mind gets respect early, and people take longer to bring you anything personal. On a first date the conversation's great and stays somehow general. When you meet someone you like, let the warmth land on them by name, and say something that's about this person in particular and would fit nobody else.
rising.reversed:
Aloof is the word people reach for when this card is reversed on an Aquarius rising. The detriment shows plainly, the Sun's warmth held so far off that you come across as detached, or a bit superior, more interested in ideas than in whoever's talking to you. You can seem unbothered, someone who doesn't need anyone, and that quietly puts people off coming closer.

At work you're seen as clever and a bit cold, consulted for your thinking and left out of the warmer stuff. The new group found you impressive and didn't think you wanted in. On the next introduction, show a flicker of ordinary warmth early, ask about them like you mean it, and let one person see you're pleased to be there.

sun.upright:
Pisces's own card is The Moon, which comes straight before The Sun in the deck, so a Pisces Sun drawing this one is being shown the next card along. You're here to feel your way towards something larger and to soften the hard edges other people insist on. The Sun is only a visitor in Pisces and takes its colour from Jupiter, or Neptune if you use the modern ruler, so its brightness reaches you soft and spread out. Leo is quincunx to Pisces, five signs apart with nothing in common, which means a constant quiet adjustment between the Sun wanting a defined self to shine as and Pisces preferring not to be pinned to one shape.

The Sun keeps asking who exactly you are, and a Pisces Sun would honestly sooner stay fluid and be several things. So your sense of self can be lovely and a bit hard to hold, strong one day and porous the next, and your energy rises and falls with your surroundings in a way sturdier signs don't understand. Around the right people your light is extraordinary. Around the wrong ones it drains, and you don't always notice until most of it's gone.

At work you have a creative or caring gift that's genuinely rare, and real trouble holding a boundary around your own time. In love you can merge so completely with a partner that you lose track of what you wanted. Keep one thing that's yours alone, a project or a plan nobody else is in.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this card reversed tends to drift. The warmth loses its outline, and the brightness slips into daydream and wishful thinking, a lovely fog where things will work out without you having to shape them. Or it turns into escape, the small ways you slip out of a life that feels too sharp, and your energy leaks away through the exits.

At work there's a deadline that stayed hazy and a talent with nothing finished to show for it. In love you see who you wish they were and miss who's actually there. There's a low, foggy tiredness to it, of never quite landing in your own life. Choose something real and small, a shelf to put up, a form to send, and do it all the way to the end.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon picks up everyone's weather, and its own gets mixed in with the rest. You take in the mood of a room through your skin, and what soothes you is retreat, water, music, sleep, some way to let the day's absorbed feelings drain back out. The Sun takes on Jupiter's colours here, or Neptune's, so the gladness it brings is tender and a bit boundless, the kind that can well up while you're watching a stranger be kind to someone.

Leo is quincunx to Pisces, and the fit is awkward. Leo would have you claim your joy out loud and be seen in it, and a Pisces Moon isn't even sure which feelings are its to claim, because so much of what you carry was picked up from somebody else. The real work here is telling your own feelings apart from the crowd's. When you're low it's worth asking whose low it is, because half the time it came from a friend, a partner or the news, and you took it for your own.

With a partner you feel their bad day so completely that you forget to check on yours. Friends offload onto you, and you go home heavy without knowing why. Your body needs water, quiet and long sleep to reset, and it pays when it doesn't get them. Before you take a mood as yours, ask where you were and who you were with when it arrived, and give the borrowed ones back.
moon.reversed:
The edges dissolve too far. With the card upside down, a Pisces Moon loses track of where it ends and everyone else begins, flooded with feeling and no way to sort it, and the pull towards numbing it, whatever your version of that is, gets strong. The warmth is somewhere behind a fog you can't reach through.

Your partner's every mood gets absorbed until there's no self left to bring. With friends you give and give with nothing coming back and call it love. Your body goes towards escape, oversleeping, a low tide that won't turn. Do one small, solid, physical thing to find the edge of yourself again, cold water on your face, a walk, a cooked meal, and tell somebody plainly that you're not okay.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising is hard to pin down on sight, soft-edged, a bit dreamy, changeable, someone people find gentle and can't quite describe afterwards. The Sun has no rank to speak of in your rising sign and works through Neptune, so the warmth you give off is diffuse and receptive, a general glow, and you tend to take on some of the colour of whoever you're standing next to.

The quincunx from Leo means a small, ongoing adjustment. The card would have you arrive as one clear, warm self, and a Pisces doorway shifts to match the room, mirroring the person in front of you so naturally you barely notice you're doing it. People meet a lovely, adaptable warmth and often leave not quite sure who they met. From the inside it feels like kindness, meeting people where they are. It can also mean you never quite turn up as anybody in particular, and that costs you.

At a first meeting you're warm and easy and leave no clear impression of yourself. In a new job you blend in so well that nobody learns what you're actually good at. In dating you become a bit of what the other person wants and lose your own sense of whether you even like them. When you meet someone new, hold one edge of yourself steady, one clear opinion or want, and don't let it blur to match theirs.
rising.reversed:
Vague, or not quite reliable, is how Pisces rising can come across with this card reversed. Neptune on the doorway, upside down, has you saying yes because it's easier than being clear, and then quietly not turning up. Or you take on so much of other people's colour that new acquaintances get a slightly different you each time, and can't find anything solid to hold on to.

At work you get a reputation for being lovely and slightly hard to count on. Socially you agree to things you didn't want because a clear no felt too sharp. With someone new, your signals shift with your mood and they end up unsure where they stand. At the next meeting, say one plain, definite thing and stick to it, even if it's only a yes or no that you actually mean.

1.upright:
Your body, the way you carry it, and how you start things all belong to the first house. Its natural sign is Aries, and the Sun is exalted in Aries, so the card is welcomed here, about as well received as it gets outside its own ground. It's an angular house too, a corner of the chart, and whatever sits here shows. People are going to notice you.

What that tends to feel like is energy in the body you can actually use, and a readiness to take up your full space in a room without first checking whether that's alright. Mars is the natural ruler here and Mercury has its joy in this house, so there's a quickness to it, first moves and fast answers. The exalted Sun can run a bit too pleased with itself, though. It's easy to be so busy being seen that you don't notice who isn't keeping up, a friend, a colleague, the person walking next to you.

In the body it's a good stretch for taking on something physical and sticking with it, a sport, a long walk every morning, getting properly fit. In how you look and present, people may start treating you as someone in charge, whether or not you are. In anything new, going first will feel easier. Start the thing you've been circling, and let being seen doing it be part of the point.
1.reversed:
In the first house, a reversed Sun usually shows up in the body first. Energy runs flat and stays flat, or it runs hot on nerves and coffee. It gets into how you present, too. Either you keep yourself in the background, dressed not to be noticed, or you turn the confidence up past what you feel, because being plainly seen feels risky.

It shows in how you start things, hanging back from a new project you'd be good at, or charging in with a bravado that doesn't match how you feel inside. With new people it's shrinking or performing, and both keep them from meeting you. Get the basics back first, sleep, food, daylight, a walk. Then pick one small thing to start in front of other people, and don't dress it up.

2.upright:
Money is the obvious part of the second house, the income, the savings, the bills. The other part is what you reckon you're worth, and the two are closer than most people like to admit. Taurus is the house's natural sign, ruled by Venus, and it's a succedent house, the kind that builds up and holds on to what it's built. The Sun brings warmth and confidence into that, and it can show as money moving more easily or as a steadier sense of your own value. Usually the two turn up together.

There's some friction, though. Leo squares Taurus, both fixed signs, and here the square is a tug between wanting to spend so people can see you're doing well and wanting to hold on to what you've got. The Sun likes generosity and a bit of show, the round of drinks, the gift that's slightly too nice. Taurus likes the balance to stay where it is. Most people with this card in the second end up doing some of each and feeling a bit guilty about both.

With income it's a good placement for asking to be paid what you're worth, or for putting your prices up if you work for yourself. With spending it favours things that last and give you pleasure for years, good boots, a decent bed, a course. With self-worth it's a quieter confidence that holds even in a thin month. Work out what an hour of your time is actually worth and write the figure down where you'll see it.
2.reversed:
Money and mood get tied together when the Sun is reversed in the second house. You feel bright when the account's healthy and flat when it isn't, and the swing is bigger than the numbers deserve. Or the spending gets a bit showy, the dinner you insisted on paying for, the upgrade you didn't need, because in the moment it felt like proof you were doing fine. The fixed square from Leo can also turn it into a tight grip, every dollar kept where it is and none of it enjoyed.

It shows on the statement, and in how you feel when you open the banking app. It shows in self-worth that rises and falls with a pay cheque. Go through the last month of spending and mark each item with how it made you feel a week later. Keep the ones that still feel good, and drop one that doesn't.

3.upright:
