Messages, siblings, the neighbours, the drive to the shops, whatever you're learning. That's third house territory. It's a cadent house, where things get processed and taken in. Gemini and Mercury are its natural sign and ruler, and the Moon has its joy here, so it's busy, chatty, curious ground. Leo is sextile to Gemini, fire and air two signs apart, and the Sun gets on well enough with all of it.

What you'll probably notice is that talking to people goes better. You explain things clearly, you're warmer on the phone, the awkward email gets written without three drafts. It can feel like being properly understood for once, and that tends to make you braver about saying what you think. The Sun likes to be at the centre, though, and in a house full of conversation that can turn into doing most of the talking. Let the other person finish their sentences, even when you know where they're going.

With a brother or sister, ring for no reason, or sort out something old in one straightforward conversation. Around your local area you might become a regular somewhere, or start a short course that turns out to suit you. Anything you're learning will go in better if you can talk it through out loud with someone. Call the sibling or old neighbour you keep meaning to call.
3.reversed:
In the third house a reversed Sun often shows as a flatness in how you talk to people. Replies get left for days, the phone stays on silent, and even a short call feels like work. Or it goes the other way and you're chattering brightly in the group chat so nobody notices you haven't actually said anything. Mercury rules this house and likes things moving, so a stall here tends to leave you feeling slow and a bit stupid, which you aren't.

It tends to show with siblings and neighbours, in the easy chat that never gets to what's actually wrong. It shows in learning too, a course dropped as soon as it stops being fun, and in errands you put off because they mean talking to someone. Answer the three oldest messages in your phone, briefly and honestly, and see how much lighter it feels.

4.upright:
Home, in every sense, is the fourth house. Where you live, who raised you, and what happens behind your own front door. Cancer is the sign that naturally sits here, and the Moon rules it. It's an angular house, a corner of the chart, so what happens here sets the tone for everything else, and with the Sun drawn into it, a lot of your energy is going into home.

Leo and Cancer sit next to each other and have little in common. Leo wants to be looked at. Cancer wants somewhere private to be. So the Sun at the base of your chart can pull two ways. You may want to do the place up, have people round, make it somewhere you're proud of, and also feel oddly protective of it when they arrive. There's often something about family in it too, an old role you played as a child, the one who kept everyone cheerful, say, and whether you're still playing it.

In the house itself it's a good stretch for making one room properly bright, painting it, moving the furniture towards the window, getting rid of what's been there too long. With parents or siblings there may be a warmer conversation than you've had in a while, or a family gathering that actually goes well. Have people over for a meal, even if the place isn't finished.
4.reversed:
The Sun reversed in the fourth house tends to mean home has gone a bit grey. It might be the actual place, dark and cluttered, somewhere you don't much enjoy coming back to. Or it's the feeling in it, a household where everyone's tired and nobody's had a proper laugh together in a while. The Moon rules this house, and the mood at home tends to follow whoever's feeling lowest.

It shows in family roles that haven't been updated in twenty years, and in a sense of dread before a family occasion. It shows in never inviting anyone round because the place isn't ready. Open the curtains, clear one surface properly, and have one person over, even if it's only for a cup of tea.

5.upright:
The fifth house belongs to the Sun. Leo is its natural sign and the Sun its natural ruler, so the card is on home turf here, and Venus has her joy in the fifth as well. It covers romance, creative work, children, hobbies, sport, parties, whatever you do purely because you enjoy it. It's a succedent house, and what gets built here tends to stay built.

There's not much friction to report, which is rare and worth making the most of. You might find you want to make something, a painting, a song, a garden, and that it comes easily. Romance can feel lighter and more fun, and if there's someone you like, it's easier to say so. The only real risk is that it's all so easy you let it stay a feeling, the novel you think about, the date you nearly suggest. The Sun here gives you the energy to actually do the fun thing.

With children, yours or a niece or a friend's kids, it's being the adult who gets on the floor and joins in the game. In romance it's making a real plan, dinner somewhere good, a whole day out. In creative work it's finishing something and showing it to someone. Book the class, the gig or the day off you'd enjoy most, and go.
5.reversed:
Reversed in its own house, the Sun usually means the fun has dried up. The fifth is where joy should come easiest, so it stings more when it doesn't. The hobby has become a chore, the creative project's in a drawer, romance has settled into logistics. Or the fun has turned into showing off, the party thrown to be seen throwing it, the relationship kept going for how it looks.

It shows at weekends that don't feel like weekends, and in how little you play with the children in your life. A creative block here is usually fear of being judged, and has little to do with ideas. Take the unfinished thing out of the drawer, give it one evening, and show whatever comes of it to one person who'll be kind.

6.upright:
Work as in the job you do each day, and health as in the upkeep, are both sixth house matters. So are the routines that keep you going, the washing up and the dog walk. Virgo belongs here naturally, with Mercury as ruler, and Mars has its joy in this house, which makes it practical and fairly effortful ground. It's a cadent house, where things get adjusted and maintained. The Sun doesn't often spend much time down here, and when it does, it brings energy to the dull parts of life.

Leo and Virgo sit next to each other with little in common, one wanting to be seen and the other wanting to be useful, and you might feel that in your working day. The Sun wants your effort noticed. The sixth house mostly goes unnoticed by design, the invisible work that keeps things running. It can make you a bit restless with routine, or keen to do the job better than it needs so someone will see. At its best, though, the Sun here makes ordinary days feel worth getting up for.

In the body it's a good stretch to build a habit that gives you energy back, morning light, a regular walk, eating lunch away from the desk. At work you may get more done in less time and enjoy it more. With colleagues you can be the one who makes the place better to be in. Pick one habit that leaves you with energy to spare, and do it at the same time every day.
6.reversed:
In the sixth house, a reversed Sun often shows as working days with no light in them. The routine gets heavier, you push on through tiredness with caffeine and good intentions, and the small things that used to keep you well, the walk, the early night, the proper lunch, drop out one by one. Mars has its joy here, and with the Sun reversed that effort can turn into grinding. Or the habits go strict and joyless, exercise as punishment, a diet that makes you miserable.

It shows at work as long days that don't achieve much, and in the body as a tiredness sleep doesn't fix. A pet or a pot plant might be the only thing getting regular care. Put back one restoring habit, the one you enjoyed most, and let the rest of the list wait.

7.upright:
Whoever sits across the table from you as an equal lives in the seventh house. A partner, a husband or wife, a business partner, anyone you've made a serious one-to-one agreement with. It's an angular house, so what happens here is visible and it matters. Libra is the natural sign, Venus the ruler, and the Sun is in fall in Libra, which means the card's way of working runs against what this house wants. The Sun wants to shine as itself. The seventh house wants two people meeting halfway.

It's worth being honest about that friction. With the Sun here, one person in a partnership can end up as the bright one, the one whose plans and moods set the day, while the other fades a bit without either of you choosing it. It might be you doing the shining, or it might be them. That's what the fall looks like in a relationship, and it means the warmth has to be shared on purpose, because it won't happen by itself. Leo is sextile to Libra, which helps, since there's real goodwill to work with.

With a partner this can be a warm, generous stretch, especially if you let them have the spotlight sometimes. In business it's a partnership where one of you is the public face, and it helps to agree which one. You might meet someone who's very much this card, confident, warm, a lot of fun. Ask your partner what they'd like more of from you, and listen to the whole answer.
7.reversed:
Somebody's plans always win when the Sun is reversed in the seventh house. One person's bad mood runs the evening, the other has gone a bit quiet, and neither of you quite remembers agreeing to it. Or the warmth has gone out of things altogether and you're both being pleasant, polite and slightly lonely. The Sun is in fall in Libra, this house's natural sign, and reversed it can struggle to meet anyone as an equal.

It shows in who decides where you go on holiday, and whose friends you mostly see. In business it's a partner who takes the credit, or one who never gets any. In a contract it can mean terms that looked generous and turned out lopsided. Let the other person choose the next three things you do together, and go along with them properly.

8.upright:
Joint money, debts, the mortgage, an inheritance, intimacy and sex, and the endings a life goes through. The eighth house covers what you share with someone at the deepest level. Scorpio is the house's own sign, with Mars as its traditional ruler and Pluto as the modern one. It's a succedent house, where things build up and are held, and by nature it's private. The Sun isn't a private planet, so this is a card being asked to shine somewhere that usually keeps the lights low.

Leo is square to Scorpio, both fixed, and in this house the square is a tug between wanting everything out in the open and wanting to guard it. You might find you're ready to talk about things you normally wouldn't, what you owe, what you want from closeness, what you're afraid of losing, and a bit alarmed at yourself for wanting to. Usually the talking goes better than you expected. The eighth house holds a lot of old embarrassment, and talking about it plainly usually shrinks it.

With a partner's money it's a good time to get everything written down where you can both see it. In intimacy it's a warmer, more honest closeness, with more laughter in it. With an ending, if something has run its course, it's letting it end kindly. Have the money conversation you've been avoiding, with the actual figures in front of you.
8.reversed:
Reversed in the eighth house, the Sun usually means something shared is being kept in the dark. A debt one of you hasn't mentioned, a joint account nobody looks at, a will that was never written. In intimacy it can be a closeness that's become routine, or one where a worry about money or about your body keeps getting in the way. The square from Leo makes it harder, since part of you would like it all out in the open and the rest of you won't go first.

It tends to show around money shared with a partner or family, and around an ending you're pretending isn't happening. Grief can go this way too, a brave face that's lasted months. Write every shared debt, account and arrangement you're part of on one page, and show it to the person who shares them.

9.upright:
The Sun has its joy in the ninth house, which is the old way of saying this is where it does its best and happiest work. The house covers travel, study, belief, the law, publishing, anything that takes you further than your own suburb and makes you wonder what it's all for. Sagittarius is the sign that belongs here, ruled by Jupiter, and Leo is trine to Sagittarius, fire to fire. So this is one of the best places in the chart for the Sun to land, with very little friction to speak of.

What it tends to feel like is a lift in your outlook. Plans for the future look possible, and you might want to go somewhere new, learn something serious, or finally commit to something you believe in. It's a cadent house, one that takes things in and learns from them, and people with the Sun here often find their confidence grows with what they study. The risk with this much ease is getting carried away. Big plans get made on a good afternoon and forgotten by the following week.

With travel it's a good time to book the trip you've talked about for years, and to plan it properly. With study it's the course or qualification that would actually change your work, and you'll probably enjoy it. With belief, whatever form yours takes, it might mean finding other people who share it, a group, a class, a congregation. Choose one bigger plan and do the first dull practical step, the form, the deposit, the email.
9.reversed:
In its own house of joy, the Sun reversed tends to mean optimism has got a bit loud. Beliefs harden into certainty, the plan gets bigger every time you describe it, and questions start to feel like attacks. Jupiter rules this house and makes everything bigger, a mood included. Or it goes the other way, a flatness about the future, the trip cancelled again, the course not started, a feeling that bigger things are for other people.

It shows in study, in chasing a big idea without doing the reading. It shows in arguments about politics or religion with someone you love, where being right has started to matter most. It shows in travel plans that never get dates. Take one belief you hold strongly and read the best argument against it you can find, all the way through.

10.upright:
Your career sits at the top of the chart in the tenth house, along with your reputation and what you're known for by people who don't know you well. The house's natural sign is Capricorn, ruled by Saturn, and it's angular, one of the four corners, so whatever lands here gets seen. The Sun in the tenth is about as visible as a card can be. Recognition is likely, and so is being asked to step up.

Leo is quincunx to Capricorn, five signs apart with nothing in common, and there's a small ongoing adjustment in it. The Sun wants to shine because it enjoys shining. Saturn wants the shine earned, and useful, and ideally with a title attached. You might feel it as a pull between the parts of your work you love and the parts that get you promoted, and they aren't always the same parts. It's worth knowing which is which before someone offers you more of the second.

At work this is a good placement for putting yourself forward, for the promotion, the bigger client, the talk at the conference. Your reputation may get a lift, sometimes from something you did years ago that's finally being noticed. With a boss or anyone senior, let them see what you can actually do. Write down what you'd most like to be known for in five years, and do one thing that points that way.
10.reversed:
Sunday nights tell you most about the Sun reversed in the tenth house. The title might be good and the job might look great from outside, and still the actual work doesn't warm you at all. Or it's the reverse, years of excellent work without anyone senior knowing your name, because putting yourself forward feels like showing off. Saturn rules the tenth, and it's quite happy for you to keep working hard at something that doesn't suit you.

It shows at work, in the gap between how things look and how they feel. It can show with a parent whose idea of success you've been living up to. Write down the three parts of your job you'd keep if nobody could see you do them, and look for a way to do more of those.

11.upright:
Friends, groups, networks and the hopes you have for the future make up the eleventh house. It takes Aquarius as its natural sign and Saturn as its traditional ruler, Uranus as its modern one. The Sun is in detriment in Aquarius, so the card is working against the grain here. The Sun wants to be the centre, and the eleventh house is about everyone together with nobody in the middle.

That's a real friction and you'll probably feel it. You may find yourself becoming the heart of a group, the one who organises, the one people ring, and then feeling uneasy about how much attention that brings. Or you want some recognition from your friends and feel slightly ashamed of wanting it. Jupiter has its joy in this house, and that helps, since there's generosity on both sides here. It's a succedent house, and friendships built in a stretch like this tend to last.

With friends this is the time to host, to get people together, to be the one who suggests the weekend away. In a group or community project you may be asked to lead, and it's fine to say yes. With your hopes it's letting yourself want something bigger for your own future, and saying so to a friend who'll take it seriously. Get the old group together, even if it takes six attempts to find a date.
11.reversed:
In the eleventh house a reversed Sun often means you're carrying a group that doesn't carry you. You organise the dinners, remember the birthdays and keep the group chat going, and it's been a long time since anyone asked how you are. The detriment shows plainly here, the Sun spending itself on the group until there's not much left for you. Or it tips the other way, and you need to be the most important person in every room, and friends have started getting together without telling you.

It shows in which friends you'd call in a crisis, and whether they'd call you. It shows in hopes for the future that have been on hold so long you've stopped mentioning them. Turn down the next thing you'd normally organise, and see who picks it up.

12.upright:
Sleep, rest, dreams and the things you keep to yourself belong to the twelfth house, the most private corner of the chart. Pisces is the sign that goes with it, with Jupiter as traditional ruler and Neptune as modern, and Saturn has its joy here. Being cadent, it's where things get let go of. The Sun is a public planet by nature, so drawing it into the twelfth is a bit like finding a lamp left on in a back room.

Leo and Pisces are a quincunx apart, which makes for an odd fit. The Sun wants to be seen, and the twelfth house is where nobody's looking, so what's live here tends to be private. It can be a good mood that seems to come from nowhere and doesn't need anyone to share it. It can be an old worry that finally loosens because you've looked at it squarely. Saturn's joy here means structure helps, a regular bedtime, a protected hour, a practice you keep to.

Your nights may be worth sorting out properly, the dark room, the phone left in the kitchen. With dreams it's worth keeping a notebook by the bed, since they may be unusually clear. With anyone you help quietly, a relative in care, a friend through a hard time, the help goes further than you'd guess. Take a day completely on your own, and don't tell anyone what you did with it.
12.reversed:
Rest that doesn't rest you is the usual sign of the Sun reversed in the twelfth house. The weekend in bed leaves you more tired, the late-night scrolling goes on an hour too long, and whatever you do to switch off soothes without actually restoring anything. The quincunx from Leo makes the Sun awkward here, wanting to be seen in a house built for staying out of sight, and reversed it can simply go into hiding.

It shows in sleep that doesn't refresh you, and in a tiredness you've stopped mentioning. It can show as avoiding friends without quite knowing why, or as a private good feeling you keep to yourself because you're not sure you're allowed it. Take one full day of proper rest with daylight in it, and tell someone you trust how you've really been.
